texts.value: Potent antimicrobial peptide with activity against Gram-positive bacteria (S.aureus (MIC=0.7-3.79 uM), S.epidermis (MIC=0.7 uM) and S.sanguinis (MIC=10.9 uM)), Gram-negative bacteria (E.coli (MIC=1.41-7.81 uM), A.actinomycetemcomitans (MIC=10.6 uM), P.aeruginosa (MIC=2.82 uM), A.baumannii (MIC=0.7 uM) and multidrug-resistant (MDR) K.pneumoniae strains (MIC=2-8 uM)), and yeasts (C.krusei (MIC=26.3 uM) and C.neoformans (MIC=13.2 uM)) (Probable) (PubMed:19946788, PubMed:27989223, PubMed:33175610, PubMed:40430498). Also reduces metabolic activity of Gram-positive and Gram-negative periodontal cells as well as of multispecies biofilm bacteria (PubMed:27989223). Has moderate hemolytic activity (PubMed:19946788). Forms pores in lipid bilayers in vitro; pore formation is reduced when cholesterol is present in the bilayers (PubMed:19946788). In vivo, in a murine pneumonia model, intraperitoneal injection reduces the bacterial load and inflammation in the lungs of animals (PubMed:40430498)

In a hydrophobic environment, adopts an amphipathic alpha-helical conformation with a small random-coil region near the N-terminus; in aqueous environments, assumes a random coil conformation (PubMed:19946788, PubMed:39858352). Interacts parallel to the membrane surface (PubMed:39858352)
Expressed by the venom gland

mnDeltaK-LyeTxI as a promising infection-specific PET radiotracer candidate. The synthetic peptide mnDeltaK-LyeTxI labeled with Gallium-68 is a promising peptide for molecular imaging of infections through positron emission tomography (PET). It effectively distinguishes bacterial infection from aseptic inflammation sites (PubMed:39426352). It is a minimized version of LyeTxI (AA 1-15) with an additional Lys in the middle of the sequence and an amidated Lys-15 (PubMed:33175610)

mnDeltaK-LyeTxI as a promising candidate for antimicrobial agent development. The synthetic peptide mnDeltaK-LyeTxI is a promising molecule for the development of new antimicrobial agents (PubMed:33175610). It is a minimized version of LyeTxI (AA 1-15) with an additional Lys in the middle of the sequence and an amidated Lys-15 (PubMed:33175610). Shows reduced hemolytic and neurotoxic activities, and a reduced antimicrobial activity. In vivo, in a mouse model of septic arthritis induced by S.aureus, is able to reduce infection, with decrease of inflammatory process and pain (PubMed:33175610). Shows a potent activity against Candida spp. with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum fungicide concentration (MFC) between 4 and 32 uM. Also completely inhibits the yeast-to-hypha transition and breaks mature biofilms of C.albicans (PubMed:35731024). Shows remarkable efficacy against planktonic cells (MIC 8-16 uM) and biofilms (>30% of inhibition) of methicillin-resistant S.aureus (MRSA) (PubMed:38534683)

LyeTxI-b as a promising candidate for antibiotic development (PubMed:29681894, PubMed:30987317). LyeTxI-b is similar to LyeTxI with an additional acetylation at Ile-1 and a deletion of His-16 (PubMed:29681894). Shows a potent antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative planktonic bacteria, being 10-fold more active than the native peptide against Escherichia coli. In vivo, in a mouse model of septic arthritis induced by S.aureus, is able to reduce infection (PubMed:29681894). Could also be used to treat resistant bacterial keratitis since it shows effective antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activity (PubMed:30987317)

LyeTxI-b as a promising candidate for anticancer drug development (PubMed:30449002, PubMed:35601827). LyeTxI-b is similar to LyeTxI with an additional acetylation at Ile-1 and a deletion of His-16 (PubMed:29681894). Shows anticancer properties by killing glioblastoma lineage U87-MG cells primarily through a membranolytic mechanism, causing rapid plasma membrane disruption and holes or pore formation, leading to necroptosis (PubMed:30449002). Exhibits potent cytotoxic effects, either alone or in combination with the anticancer drug cisplatin, against triple-negative breast cancer cell lines. Cells treated with this combination are arrested in the G2/M phase and show markers indicating autophagic cell death (PubMed:35601827)
Belongs to the cationic peptide 04 (cupiennin) family. 05 subfamily

texts.value: Pore-forming protein that forms cations-selective hydrophilic pores of around 1 nm and causes cardiac stimulation and cytolysis. Pore formation is a multi-step process that involves specific recognition of membrane sphingomyelin (but neither cholesterol nor phosphatidylcholine) using aromatic rich region and adjacent phosphocholine (POC) binding site, firm binding to the membrane (mainly driven by hydrophobic interactions) accompanied by the transfer of the N-terminal region to the lipid-water interface and finally pore formation after oligomerization of monomers. Cytolytic effects include red blood cells hemolysis, platelet aggregation and lysis, cytotoxic and cytostatic effects on fibroblasts. Lethality in mammals has been ascribed to severe vasospasm of coronary vessels, cardiac arrhythmia, and inotropic effects
Octamer or nonamer in membranes. Monomer in the soluble state
Forms an alpha-helical membrane channel in the prey

Composed of a long N-terminal alpha-helix and a core region rich in beta-sheet structures. Before the pore formation, the alpha-helix binds the lipid membrane, partitions into the lipid-water interface and stabilizes the monomeric molecule on the membrane. Finally, it traverses the bilayer, thus forming the transmembrane pore
LD(50) is 23 ug/kg by intravenous injection into mice
Belongs to the actinoporin family. Sea anemone subfamily

texts.value: Nerve growth factor is important for the development and maintenance of the sympathetic and sensory nervous systems. Binds a lipid between the two protein chains in the homodimer. The lipid-bound form promotes histamine relase from mouse mast cells, contrary to the lipid-free form (By similarity)
